units.function: Ten mocked route tests for CLI authorization challenges, invite-scoped Skill retrieval, challenge approval, board API key creation/list/revocation and activity fan-out.
units.dependencyDirection: Supertest/Express -> real access route/authz/error composition -> fully mocked Access, Agent, BoardAuth and activity services; no real database, session middleware, token hashing or key persistence.
units.keyDataModels: CLI auth challenge/secret, pending board token, requested access/company, signed-in board actor, named board API key, expiry and per-company activity records.
units.lifecycle: Anonymous client creates challenge and receives polling/approval material -> user signs in and approves -> client uses pending board key -> users create/list/revoke long-lived named keys -> activity is projected to resolved companies.
units.testAssessment: Sandboxed focused Vitest failed 10/10 solely because Supertest listen was denied with EPERM. The approved unsandboxed rerun passed all 10/10. This proves route response/service-call composition under mocks, not authorization, storage, cryptography, expiry/replay or real audit durability.
units.designRationale: A browser-mediated authorization challenge avoids asking users to paste session cookies into CLI tools and provides an approval ceremony for operator credentials.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs standards-based CLI/device authorization with product-specific audience, tenant/capability scope, short expiry, one-time exchange, revocation and accountable approval evidence.
units.companyOsFit: REIMPLEMENT through IdentityPort using OAuth/OIDC Device Authorization or an equivalent standards-shaped flow. Return a short user code/verification URI, keep the eventual credential server-side until one-time exchange, bind requested audience/company/capabilities and command digest, and issue short-lived tokens plus rotatable refresh authority. Adapt only the explicit approval/status UX and activity intent.
units.responsibilityConflict: Credential approval is logged but not bound in these tests to an exact operator action, role separation or responsibility contract. A board credential represents broad user authority rather than a scoped approval for high-risk work.
evidence: 2026-08-19 sandboxed Vitest: 10/10 failed from listen EPERM
units.securityFindings: CRITICAL design concern: anonymous challenge creation returns both the challenge secret in URL/query material and pendingBoardToken in the initial response, exposing the future bearer credential before human approval; tests do not prove it is unusable before approval, one-time, bound to the initiating client or erased after exchange. Query secrets can leak through history, logs, analytics and referrers. HIGH: requestedCompanyId is passed when creating the route request and resolving audit companies, but createNamedBoardApiKey is called only with userId/name/expiresAt, so the credential itself is not proven company-scoped. Named keys may have expiresAt=null and plaintext bearer token is returned; no one-time-display assertion exists. Missing negative cases include unauthorized/other-company approval, stale/expired/cancelled/replayed/wrong secrets, concurrent approvals, challenge enumeration/rate limit, CSRF/session freshness/MFA, token hashing, scope escalation, revoked-key use, audit failure transactionality and stable error codes. Anonymous invite Skill testing uses a fully mocked DB and does not prove token hashing/revocation or tenant filtering.
